body.text: 6. bhagavan paramāścaryaṃ sugata | yāvad ayaṃ dharmaparyāyas tathāgatena bhāṣito yato me bhagavaṃ jñānam utpannaṃ na me jātv ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ śrūtapūrvaḥ parameṇa
body.translated_text: 6. <s>Bhagavān</s>! Supremely wonderful, <s>Sugata</s>! This <s>Dharma</s> discourse has been spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; from it knowledge has arisen in me. Never before have I heard such a <s>Dharma</s> discourse. With the utmost

body.text: 4. | tat kasya hetoḥ paramapāramiteyaṃ subhūte tathāgatena bhāṣitā| yāṃ ca tathāgataḥ paramapāramitāṃ bhāṣate | tām aparimāṇā buddhā bhagavanto bhāṣante | te
body.translated_text: 4. Why? Because this, <s>Subhūti</s>, has been called the supreme <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And what the <s>Tathāgata</s> calls the supreme <s>pāramitā</s>, that immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> also declare; there-

body.text: 5. // api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte ya tathāgatasya kṣāntipāramitā saivāpāramitā | tat kasya hetoḥ yadā subhūte kalirājāṅgapratyaṃgamāṃsāny acchaitsīt nāsī
body.translated_text: 5. Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, what is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s perfection of patience, that indeed is a non-perfection. Why? Because when King <s>Kali</s> cut my limbs and flesh, I had no

body.text: 6. me tasmin samaye ātmasaṃjñā vā satvasaṃjñā vā jīvasaṃjñā vā pudgalasaṃjñā vā | vyāpādasaṃjñā vāpi me tasmin samaye 'bhaviṣyad abhijānāmy ahaṃ subhūte atīte 'dhvani paṃca jātiśa
body.translated_text: 6. perception of self, nor perception of a being, nor perception of a soul, nor perception of a person at that time; nor did I have a perception of ill-will at that time. I recall, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the past, for five hundred

body.text: 7. yo 'haṃ kṣāntivādī ṛṣir abhūvaṃs tatrāpi me nātmasaṃjñābhūn na satvasaṃjñā na jīvasaṃjñā na pudgalasaṃjñā | tasmāt tarhi subhūte bodhisatvena mahāsatvena sarvasaṃjñā varjayitvā
body.translated_text: 7. I was the seer <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> (Preacher of Patience). Then too I had no perception of self, no perception of a being, no perception of a soul, no perception of a person. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having abandoned all perceptions,

body.text: 1. ḥrimāṇena | sarve te satvā mamāṃsena bodhiṃ dhārayiṣyanti | tat kasya hetoḥ na hi śakyaṃ subhūte ayaṃ dharmaparyāyo hīnādhimuktikaiḥ satvaiḥ śrotuṃ| nātmadṛṣṭikair na satvajīvapu
body.translated_text: 1. ...with immeasurable [merit]. All those beings will sustain <s>bodhi</s> through my flesh. Why? Because it is not possible, <s>Subhūti</s>, for this <s>Dharma</s> discourse to be heard by beings of inferior aspirations, nor by those with the view of self, nor by those with the view of a being, soul, or

body.text: 2. śakyaṃ śrotuṃ udgrahītuṃ vā | yāvat paryavāptuṃ vā nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate | api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte yatra pṛthivīpradeśe idaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśayiṣyati | pūjanīyaḥ sa
body.translated_text: 2. It is not possible for them to hear, to take up, or to fully comprehend it. This situation does not exist. Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, wherever on earth this <s>sūtra</s> will be proclaimed, that

body.text: 3. pṛthivīpradeśo bhaviṣyati | sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasya vandanīyaḥ pradakṣiṇīkaraṇīyaś caityabhūta sa pṛthivīpradeśo bhaviṣyati | ye te subhūte kulaputrā
body.translated_text: 3. spot on earth will be worthy of worship by the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>; it will be worthy of salutation and circumambulation; that spot on earth will become like a <s>caitya</s> (shrine). Those, <s>Subhūti</s>, sons of good family

body.text: 4. vā kuladuhitaro vā | imān evaṃrūpān sūtrāntān udgrahīṣyanti yāvat paryavāpsyanti | te paribhūtā bhaviṣyanti suparibhūtāḥ yāni ca teṣāṃ satvānāṃ pūrvajanmikāny aśubhāni ka
body.translated_text: 4. or daughters of good family who will take up such <s>sūtras</s> and will fully comprehend them — they will be despised and greatly despised. Yet those previous unwholesome <s>karmas</s> of those beings

body.text: 5. apāyasaṃvartanīyāni tāni dṛṣṭa eva dharme paribhūtatayā kṣapayiṣyanti buddabodhiṃ cānuprāpsyanti | abhijānāmy ahaṃ subhūte atīte 'dhvany asaṃ
body.translated_text: 5. woeful states of rebirth will, in this very life, through being despised, be exhausted, and they will attain the awakening of a <s>Buddha</s>. I recall, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the past, in incal-

body.text: 6. dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pareṇa caturaśītir buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇy abhūvan yāni mayā ārāgitāni ārāgya ca na virāgitāni |
body.translated_text: 6. <s>kalpas</s>, after the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, there were eighty-four hundred thousand million <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> who were pleased by me, and having been pleased, they were not displeased.

body.text: 1. yac ca mayā subhūte te buddhā bhagavanta ārāgya na virāgitā yac ca carime kāle paścimāyāṃ paṃcāśatyāṃ vartamānāyām imāṃ sūtrāntān udgrahīṣyanti | yāvat paryavāpsyanti | asya subhū
body.translated_text: 1. And although, <s>Subhūti</s>, those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> were pleased by me and not displeased, yet in the last time, in the last period, in the last five hundred [years], those who will take up these <s>sūtras</s> and fully comprehend them — this,

body.text: 2. puṇyaskandhasyāsau pūrvakaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ śatatamīm api kalān nopaiti | sahasratamīm api | śatasahasratamīm api | saṃkhyām api kalām api gaṇanām apy upamām apy upa
body.translated_text: 2. heap of merit [of those beings] — that earlier heap of merit does not approach even a hundredth part, or a thousandth part, or a hundred-thousandth part; it does not bear comparison, calculation, illustration, or

body.text: 3. api na kṣamate | sacet subhūte teṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitrīṇāṃ ca puṇyaskandhaṃ bhāṣeyaṃ yāvantas te satvā kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca tasmin samaye puṇya
body.translated_text: 3. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, I were to speak of the heap of merit of those sons and daughters of good family — as many beings, sons and daughters of good family, as would at that time grasp that heap of

body.text: 4. parigrahīṣyanti | unmādaṃ satvā anuprāpnuyuś cittavikṣepaṃ vā gaccheyuḥ api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte acintyo 'yaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ asyācintya eva vipākaḥ //
body.translated_text: 4. those beings would go mad or suffer mental distraction. Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>Dharma</s> discourse is inconceivable, and its fruition too is inconceivable."

body.text: 5. āha | kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisatvayānasaṃprasthitena sthātavyaṃ kathaṃ pratipattavyaṃ kathaṃ cittaṃ pragṛhītavyaṃ | bhagavān āha | iha subhūte bodhisatvayānasaṃprasthitenaivaṃ cittam utpā
body.translated_text: 5. He said: "How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should one who has set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle stand? How should one practice? How should one control the mind?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, one who has set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle should generate the mind

body.text: 6. sarvasatvā mayā anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāpayitavyāḥ evaṃ ca satvān parinirvāpya na kaścit satvaḥ parinirvāpito bhavati | tat kasya hetoḥ sace
body.translated_text: 6. 'All beings must be led by me to <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> without remainder.' And yet, having led beings to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, no being whatsoever has been led to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Why? Because if

body.text: 1. subhūte bodhisatvasya satvasaṃjñā pravarteta | jīvasaṃjñā pudgalasaṃjñā vā na sa bodhisatva iti vaktavyaḥ tat kasya hetoḥ nāsti subhūte sa dharmo yo bodhisatvayānasaṃprasthito nāma | tat kiṃ manya
body.translated_text: 1. <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> were to have the perception of a being, or the perception of a soul or of a person, he should not be called a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Why? There is no <s>dharma</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, called 'one who has set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle.' What do you think,

body.text: 2. subhūte asti sa kaścid dharmo yas tathāgatena dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyāntikād anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ āha | nāsti sa bhagavan kaścid dharmo yas tathāgatena dīpaṃkara
body.translated_text: 2. <s>Subhūti</s>? Is there any <s>dharma</s> by which the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening?" He said: "There is no such <s>dharma</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, by which the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>

body.text: 3. tathāgatasyāntikād anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ āha | tasmād ahaṃ dīpaṃkareṇa tathāgatena vyākṛto bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇavānāgate 'dhvani śākyamunir nāma tathā
body.translated_text: 3. <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening." He said: "Therefore I was predicted by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>: 'You, young man, will in the future become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>,'

body.text: 4. 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas tat kasya hetos tathāgata iti subhūte tathatāyā etad adhivacanaṃ yaḥ kaścit subhūte evaṃ vadet tathāgatenānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃbuddheti |
body.translated_text: 4. an <s>arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened. Why? '<s>Tathāgata</s>,' <s>Subhūti</s>, is a designation for <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). If anyone, <s>Subhūti</s>, were to say that the <s>Tathāgata</s> has fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening —

body.text: 5. nāsti subhūte sa kaścid dharmo yas tathāgatenānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃbuddhaḥ yaḥ subhūte tathāgatena dharmo 'bhisaṃbuddhas tatra na satyaṃ na mṛṣāḥ tasmāt tathāgato bhāṣate | sarva
body.translated_text: 5. There is no <s>dharma</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, that has been fully awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). That <s>dharma</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, which was [attained] by the <s>Tathāgata</s> —

body.text: 6. buddhadharmā iti | sarvadharmā iti subhūte sarve te adharmās tenocyante sarvadharmā iti // tadyathāpi nāma subhūte puruṣo bhaved upetakāyo mahākāyaḥ subhūtir āha | yo
body.translated_text: 6. '<s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>' — 'all <s>dharmas</s>,' <s>Subhūti</s> — all of them are non-<s>dharmas</s>; therefore they are called 'all <s>dharmas</s>.' Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a per-

body.text: 1. 'sau tathāgatena puruṣo bhāṣita upetakāyo mahākāyaḥ akāyaḥ sa bhagavaṃs tathāgatena bhāṣitas tenocyate upetakāyo mahākāyaḥ bhagavān āha | evam etat subhūte
body.translated_text: 1. That person was described by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as 'endowed with a body, a great body.' He is without a body — that, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, was stated by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; therefore he is called 'endowed with a body, a great body.'

body.text: 2. yo bodhisatva evaṃ vaded ahaṃ satvān parinirvāpayiṣyāmīti | na sa bodhisatva iti vaktavyaḥ tat kasya hetoḥ asti subhūte sa kaścid dharmo yo bodhisatvo nāma | āha | no hīdaṃ bha
body.translated_text: 2. If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to say: 'I shall lead beings to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>' — he should not be called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. For what reason? Is there, <s>Subhū-

body.text: 3. bhagavān āha | tasmāt tathāgato bhāṣate niḥsatvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ nirjīvā niṣpudgalāḥ yaḥ subhūte bodhisatva evaṃ vaded ahaṃ kṣetravyūhān niṣpādayiṣyāmīti | so 'pi tathaiva
body.translated_text: 3. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> declares: all <s>dharmas</s> are without a self (<s>niḥsattva</s>), without a life-force (<s>nirjīva</s>), without a person (<s>niṣpudgala</s>).' If, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to say thus,

body.text: 4. vaktavyaḥ tat kasya hetoḥ kṣetravyūhāḥ kṣetravyūhā iti subhūte avyūhās te tathāgatena bhāṣitās tenocyante kṣetravyūhā iti | yaḥ subhūte bodhisatvo nirātmāno dharmā nirā
body.translated_text: 4. he should not be called [a <s>Bodhisattva</s>]. For what reason? 'Field-arrays, field-arrays' — <s>Subhūti</s>, they are non-arrays, as declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; therefore they are called 'field-arrays.'
